problem: Prior VLN methods that add co-occurring modalities (text semantics, depth, etc.) to RGB tend to naively concatenate or fuse them into one representation, so each modality's distinct contribution is under-used and RGB-instruction heterogeneity persists. Depth is typically projected onto RGB coordinates rather than grounded independently.
motivation: Humans ground concrete semantic knowledge within spatial layouts. VLN agents struggle to ground landmarks in RGB scenes due to modality heterogeneity and overfit to RGB noise or bias. Treating text semantics (fine-grained, local) and depth (coarse, global) as separately grounded, hierarchical cues should improve generalization to unseen environments.
key_idea: SUSA adds view-level textual panoramas (BLIP-2 captions matched to the instruction) for local action prediction and a trajectory-level depth exploration map for global action prediction, then aggregates them hierarchically with learned branch weights and a contrastive alignment loss on top of DUET.
insight: Grounding each modality on its own beats fusing it into RGB features: the appendix comparison (Table related) shows depth exploration maps beat BEVBert/GridMM/SEAT depth use, and textual panoramas beat KERM/CONSOLE. The ablations show DSP mainly improves SPL, while TSU improves SR. Depth encoder pretraining on Gibson beats ImageNet (SPL 39.2 vs 34.6). Partial pretraining narrows the seen-unseen gap. The HAP module shows a mixed effect: it raises REVERIE test and R2R SR but lowers R2R SPL (64.85 to 62.84).
method: Salient Landmarks Extractor: frozen BLIP-2-FlanT5-xxL captions each of the 36 panorama views with the prompt 'a photo of'; the captions are encoded by the CLIP ViT-L/14@336 text encoder into a textual panorama.

Textual Semantic Selector: static matching computes word-view cosine similarity with max-pooling over words; dynamic matching uses a transformer cross-attention decoder (TCA) between view text features and instruction; the two are mixed with a balance factor δ (best 0.5).

Depth-Enhanced Exploration Mapping: GT simulator depth panoramas are encoded by a Gibson-pretrained ResNet-50 (RGB by CLIP). A weight-shared 2-layer panorama transformer is applied, and node features are average-pooled into a depth exploration map parallel to the DUET RGB topological map.
Cross-modal reasoning: a 4-layer cross-modal transformer with graph-aware self-attention (GASA) links the instruction to depth map, RGB map and RGB panorama features.

Hierarchical Aggregation and Prediction (HAP): attention pooling of the 4 representations plus the instruction; sigmoid-FFN branch weights β1..β4 fuse local (text, RGB) and global (depth, RGB) scores, followed by DUET dynamic fusion.

Training: partial pretraining (MLM, MRC, SAP, OG) that updates only the RGB-related flows, then fine-tuning with L = λ1 L_gt + L_pseudo + λ2 L_contrastive (λ1=0.2, λ2=0.8) aligning the hybrid representation E_hyb to the instruction.

setting.backbone: DUET-based transformer (trained), with frozen BLIP-2-FlanT5-xxL captioner and frozen CLIP ViT-L/14@336; ResNet-50 (Gibson-pretrained) depth encoder; BERT for instruction
setting.training_data: Standard R2R/REVERIE/SOON training data with DUET-style pretraining (100k iterations); no additional annotations or large-scale augmentation. R2R-CE is fine-tuned without pretraining.
setting.observation: Panoramic RGB (36 views) plus GT simulator depth panorama, generated captions, GPS
setting.action_space: Discrete navigable nodes in a topological graph (for R2R-CE, the DUET/SUSA planner is used inside ETPNav with waypoints)
setting.privileged: Ground-truth depth images from the Matterport3D simulator; discrete nav-graph connectivity

results: SUSA improves over DUET on REVERIE test unseen (SPL 41.5 vs 36.0, RGSPL 27.3 vs 22.0), R2R val unseen (SPL 64.8 vs 60), and SOON val unseen (SPL 30.8 vs 22.5). It also beats DUET in R2R-CE, where DUET-as-planner scores SR/SPL 51.9/41.2 on val unseen, while SUSA scores 52.7/43.6. It does not reach ETPNav (57/49) on R2R-CE, and on REVERIE test SR CONSOLE is higher (55.1).
limitations: Identical landmark captions at different locations are ambiguous, and the agent then fails to pick the right node (failure cases).
The captions cover only landmarks, not directions or actions. HAP gives inconsistent gains (R2R SPL drops, REVERIE val/test fluctuate), and extra modules add computational cost.
Uses GT simulator depth; R2R-CE was evaluated only briefly and remains below ETPNav.
